chunks: As for what Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā and Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Rifāʿah, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man afflicted with a stomach ailment and severe pain: may he enter Makkah without ihram? He said: He must not enter it except in a state of ihram.
He said: And he said: Indeed, the woodcutters and those who brought goods came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and asked him, so he permitted them to enter without ihram.
So the proper understanding of this report is that it indicates a kind of recommendation, not obligation and requirement.

key_terms.الْحَطَّابَةَ: those who gather or carry firewood
key_terms.الْمُجْتَلِبَةَ: those who bring goods or provisions from outside
key_terms.حَلَالًا: not in a state of ihram
key_terms.مُحْرِمًا: in a state of ihram for pilgrimage rites

ai.seo_question: Can a sick person enter Makkah without ihram according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses whether a person may enter Makkah without ihram, even when suffering from severe illness. The report presents an apparent prohibition, then cites a Prophetic allowance for certain workers, and concludes that the ruling here is to be understood as recommended rather than strictly obligatory.
